alert.title: payment heap usage drift — OOM risk in <2h

tool_calls.result_summary: linear climb 1.1GB -> 1.6GB over 6h, slope 80MB/h, no plateau
1 deploy 7 days ago: 'enable async retry queue'
no OOM yet; 12 INFO lines from RetryQueue showing queue size 240k and growing
1 prior incident matched: 'retry queue grew unbounded after stripe SDK upgrade' (2026-01)

hypotheses.reasoning: payment heap climbs linearly at 80MB/h with no GC reclaim. The async retry queue (introduced 7 days ago) has grown to 240k entries and is still climbing — entries are not being drained. A near-identical incident in 2026-01 had the same shape and was a queue dequeue regression. OOM is projected within ~90 minutes.

evidence.claim: Heap is climbing linearly with no plateau
RetryQueue size has reached 240k entries and is still climbing
Past incident with the same pattern: retry queue dequeue regression

hypotheses.recommended_action: Roll the largest payment pod first to relieve heap pressure; investigate RetryQueue dequeue path. Page payment lead if heap continues to climb after restart.

hypotheses.reasoning: An organic traffic increase could explain heap growth, but call volume is flat across the 6h window.

evidence.claim: payment request rate is flat across the climb

hypotheses.recommended_action: Compare call rate week-over-week only if rolling pods does not stabilize heap.

hypotheses.reasoning: External Stripe slowness could cause retry queue growth, but Stripe latency in the time window is at baseline.

evidence.claim: Stripe call latency is unchanged in the last 6h

escalation.reason: Slow leaks routinely fool single-shot diagnosis; flagging for human review and recommending preemptive pod roll.
